Police Behaving Badly

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate why police are shooting indiscriminately at motorists.

Unique Selling Point:
An interview with a father and son who came under armed attack from plain clothes policemen in unmarked cars. While driving from Nigel to Eden park on the night of Tuesday 29th of October, Luciano Volmink and his father Lucien were pursued from the N3, onto Klipriver Drive by 3 unmarked vehicles. Thinking they were about to be hijacked, Luciano sped up and drip

Script:


24 BULLETS


Text: 29 October 2019
20h30

V/O: It was a Tuesday night when Luciano Volmink and his father Lucien drove from Nigel to Eden Park to visit his granny. Travelling north on the N3, the 19-year-old was behind the wheel of his VW Polo.

Lucien: I spotted a Ford Ranger in one of the aisles in the entry. We passed the Ford Ranger and my son said Daddy, the Ford Ranger is following us.

Luciano: But he came really fast and my Father told me no, just go to the left and give way for him to pass. So I gave way and he passed me.

V/O: Luciano then took the R550 off-ramp to Lenasia.

Luciano: The Ford Ranger stopped before it, he stopped somewhere here.

Mac: Just over here?

Luciano: Yes, it’s right here. And then I took the offramp and passed him.

Lucien: As we got to the T-junction we spotted two Golf 7’s facing the Lenasia Rd. I told my son something is not right here: just yield and go.

Mac: So you then turn onto this road, right?

Luciano: Yes, when I looked into my mirror again, I saw the Golf 7s started driving also. They came really fast, and he told me don’t rush, keep to the speed limit. I started noticing they’re coming faster, and it started coming to the side of the car, like they trying to push us from the road. So he told me this looks like people that’s gonna hijack us. Increase the speed and drive to the nearest police station.

Lucien: The two Golf 7s with the Ranger was now following us. We could see that there was something wrong now here. We went to 180/200 but he was driving like really fast with his hazards on, and everything.

Mac: What made you feel like something is not right here?

Lucien: Three cars just chasing us out of nowhere, we felt this was a hijack.

V/O: This seems reasonable, given that VW Polos are one of the most hi-jacked cars in South Africa according to police statistics,

Mac: Was there any way of you knowing that perhaps it could have been police?

Lucien: It was unmarked cars. It was plain Golf 7, white cars, tinted windows, the same as the Ranger.

Mac; Is there any sign, is there any way for you to know that they’re police?

Luciano: I have no idea, not a sign of a police badge or anything on.

Mac: No blue lights, nothing?

Luciano: No blue lights, nothing.

V/O: According to Luciano they chased him for over 15 kilometers without flashing their blue lights. It was only when he turned off the R550 into Greenfields that he realized they could be police.

Luciano: And after turning right here, this is where they started putting on their lights.

Lucien: Why when we entered Greenfields only – we were like 5 minutes away from the police station – then he switch on his lights?

Luciano: I still told my father something’s not right. I’d rather just go to the police station.

Lobo: The law is very clear that when signaled by a police officer to stop, you have to stop.

V/O: Lobo das Neves is an international law enforcement expert who spent 25 years in the police services.

Lobo: We are well aware of the so-called blue light gangs that have robbed many people, attacked people, raped people as well in South Africa, and so looking at the circumstances one needs to make a good judgment on what to do. The first thing is to reduce speed. My advice also is, try and get to the police station as quickly as possible.

V/O: But it was this final stretch, through a residential area, that was the most dangerous.

Luciano: When we came here, just into Greenfields and I skipped the first stop, that’s the time they started firing shots at us.

Sfx: Gunshots

Luciano: When we turned left here, they fired two in the door.

Sfx: Gunshots

Lucien: I could actually feel, it when we turned into Eden Park on the left side. My son actually asked me Daddy are you shot, because he could feel it also.

Luciano: Up in this road it was like fireworks the way they were firing here.

V/O: It’s unclear how many rounds were fired that night, but 24 of them ended up in Luciano’s car.

Mac: Is there any excuse to pump over 20 bullets into a car that you’re chasing?

Lobo: It depends on the circumstances. If the occupants of the vehicle you’re chasing are firing back at you, then there’s almost no limit. But apparently an unarmed driver with an unarmed occupant, I don’t think there’s any justification for that.

Link: So after a terrifying 25 kilometer car chase this is where Lucien and his son came - to a police station hoping that it would be a place of safety. But this is where the nightmare continued.

Luciano: Me and my father got out with our hands in the sky, and one police started assaulting me.

Lucien: There was one cop kicking me. I actually asked them why did you do this to us? The one guy’s response was we look like suspects.

V/O: Luciano was charged with reckless and negligent driving and spent the night in Eden Park police station. His granny, Winnie Jordaan, also arrived and questioned the plain-clothes cops.

Winnie: I asked them why did you shoot? Because I know you can’t just shoot because I was a reservist for longer than 10 years. Why didn’t they stop? That’s what they asked me. I asked them how could they stop? They were in danger. They’re rude, unprofessional people – even their clothes. They don’t even have a real uniform.

Link: No uniforms, no badges, no name tags, no markings on their vehicles. So who were they?

V/O: The two Golf 7s belong to a special, undercover unit of the Gauteng Traffic Police. The arresting officer’s identity is known to us. In his statement he claims he turned on his blue lights before the chase started, and that he shot at the tyres of the Polo to try and slow it down.

The Department of Community Safety declined an interview pending a full investigation. They confirm that officers are not permitted to shoot without just cause, and that all necessary processes will follow in the event of any wrongdoing.
They advise motorists to proceed to the nearest police station if they feel unsafe or suspicious when pursued by unmarked cars,

Lucien: I’ve got no trust in any police anymore. If they can do this to us, what’s going to happen to the next person? Innocent people!

V/O: Lucien has since opened a case of assault and attempted murder.
